subject: Cinderford on-site cluster: compact node roles, storage attach order and routing envelope

Subject: Cinderford on-site cluster: inventory ask + proposed topics for preflight

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday. To make the on-site planning call productive, can you please share a quick site inventory and your preference for persistent storage attachment order? Specifically we need: rack count, ToR model, cross-connects to your colo (if any), host disk layout (NVMe count, local SSDs, SATA archival), and any constraints around air-gapped operations. An export of the asset list in CSV is perfect.

High-level items we want to cover on the call:
- Minimal cluster footprint (expected control vs worker counts) for an inference-only workload
- Node roles and scheduling constraints (dedicated NVMe/ephemeral for KV cache, separate blockstore pool for model weights)
- PVC bind order and attach expectations during rollout (pre-attach vs attach-on-demand)
- Network egress and routing envelope (expected BGP/peering or NAT)
- Backup/restore window and retention expectations (RPO/RTO targets)

If you already have the CSV, can you attach it? I also attached a short diagram of our recommended PVC binding order for similar compact footprints.

Proposed times for a 45-min planning call: Thu 6/13 10–11am PT or Fri 6/14 8–9am PT. Which works?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks, attaching the inventory you asked for. Key points up front:
- Facility: 3 racks available in our Boston colo, dual ToR (Cisco 9300), 40Gb fabric between racks, single cross connect to our cloud egress.
- Hosts: 8 servers planned for phase 1; each server has 2x NVMe (1.6TB each), 2x 2TB SATA for archiving. No dedicated HBA present; we can add iSCSI if required.
- Preference: we want model weights on blockstore (iSCSI-backed SAN) for snapshotting/backup; ephemeral NVMe for KV cache and local logs.
- Security: facility can be isolated during maintenance windows; we prefer no inbound from public internet to worker nodes (control-plane egress only).
- Retention: regulatory requirement to keep inference logs for 90 days; backups nightly with 24h retention for ephemeral and 90d for models.

Attached: cinderford_site_inventory.csv (small), floorplan sketch (sent to Joseph who will forward any cabling notes). Thu 6/13 10am PT works for the team.

Best,

Subject: Re: Cinderford on-site cluster: inventory ask + proposed topics for preflight

Quick technical readout based on Alice's inventory — inline notes and proposals: 

- Control plane: 3 control-plane nodes (HA) colocated across racks for quorum; advertise via virtual IP on ToR with /32 BGP announcement to their cross-connect. Use static IP pools for masters to simplify firewall rules.

- Workers: initial fleet = 6 worker nodes (leaving 2 spare for capacity and maintenance). Node labels:
  * node-role.kubernetes.io/master: control-plane nodes
  * node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: general inference workers
  * topology.kubernetes.io/zone: rack-A/B/C for failure domain awareness

- Storage: recommended split:
  * NVMe (local) -> fast ephemeral storage for KV cache + local logs. Mount as ephemeral dir; do not rely on for durable model weights.
  * Blockstore (iSCSI or SAN) -> model weights and checkpoints. Because the site prefers blockstore for snapshotting, we should configure a StorageClass that enforces ReadWriteMany if the backend supports it, otherwise ReadWriteOnce with a PV-per-node pattern and a model-sync agent to keep a consistent copy.

- PVC attach order (pv-binding-diagram.pdf):
  1) Pre-provision model PVs on blockstore and validate mount on a staging worker (pre-attach test).
  2) Bring up control plane and core services (kube-system) with local ephemeral mounts.
  3) Roll worker nodes in small batches, attach blockstore PVs after node joins to avoid kubelet attach storms.
  4) Enable delayed mount for large model files (lazy restore) to prevent initial attach congestion.

- Networking/routing envelope: NAT egress from control-plane subnets only; workers to be outbound-only. BGP to their ToR is preferred — we'll provide suggested prefixes and peering config.

- Backups: Nightly snapshot of blockstore volumes (incremental) with weekly full snapshot. For critical models, snapshot before deployment during rollout window (we will coordinate).

I'll prepare a short playbook for the rollout sequence and an ops checklist for the on-site team. Anything I missed?

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Alice —

Appreciate the quick inventory. Karthik's notes look good; below is a short mutual action plan ahead of Thu's call (6/13 10am PT):

Action items before call:
- Cinderford: confirm whether your blockstore backend supports RWX snapshots or is RWX via cluster filesystem; send any SAN iSCSI credentials we should plan for (Alice) — due 6/12 EOD.
- Redwood (Karthik/Neha): draft rollout playbook (node bringup + PV attach order) and a short BGP peering template for the ToR — due 6/13 8am PT.
- Joint: validate pre-attach test procedure on one staging worker during on-site window (Joseph will coordinate cabling/time).

Couple inline clarifications from my side on Karthik's plan:
- We'll recommend pre-provisioning model PVs and running a mount validation script prior to rolling the worker batch that will host models — that avoids large attach spikes.
- For retention: nightly incremental snapshots + a 90d retention policy for model stores; ephemeral NVMe logs rotated and shipped to their archival SATA per retention requirements.

I've attached the PV binding diagram again for reference. Looking forward to the call — invite is out for Thu 6/13 10am PT.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
